# `silk/platform/native/time_zone`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Direct reads of the time zone files and settings of a Unix system, for the native zone
providers.

## When to use
`silk.time.zones_native` uses [`NativeTimeZone`](#NativeTimeZone). Application code uses those providers
through the `TimeZones` and `LocalZone` effects, so a test can replace them.

## Details
Zone files are looked for in the directory that the variable `TZDIR` names, then in
`/usr/share/zoneinfo`, `/var/db/timezone/zoneinfo`, `/usr/lib/zoneinfo`,
`/usr/share/lib/zoneinfo`, and `/etc/zoneinfo`. The first directory that has the file wins.

The local zone is the value of the variable `TZ`, or the zone that the link `/etc/localtime`
points to, or the first line of `/etc/timezone`.

## Gotchas
- The names are not checked here. The caller must check a name with `TimeZones.isValidName`
  before it reads a file, so that a name cannot leave the zone directory.
- This module exists on Darwin x86_64 or aarch64 and on GNU Linux x86_64 or aarch64.

Import as `NativeTimeZone` with `import silk.platform.native.time_zone { NativeTimeZone }`.

Public declarations: 1.

<a id="NativeTimeZone.impl.readZoneFile"></a>

### Associated function `readZoneFile`

```silk
pub effect fn readZoneFile(name: &[u8]) -> Option<Bytes> ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the contents of the file `name` of the zone directory, such as `Europe/Rome` or
`tzdata.zi`, or `None` if no zone directory has a readable file with that name.

#### Gotchas
`name` is joined to the directory as it is. Check it with `TimeZones.isValidName` first.

#### Errors
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the contents.

<a id="NativeTimeZone.impl.localName"></a>

### Associated function `localName`

```silk
pub effect fn localName() -> Option<Bytes> ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the name of the zone that the system is set to, or `None` if the system does not
say.

#### Details
A set `TZ` variable wins: a leading `:` is removed, a path into a zone directory gives the
part after `zoneinfo/`, and an empty value means `UTC`. Without `TZ`, the answer is the part
after `zoneinfo/` of the target of the link `/etc/localtime`, and then the first line of
`/etc/timezone`. The name is not checked against the zone files, and a `TZ` value can be a
POSIX rule and not a name.

#### Errors
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the name.
